title: Archerfish, rainbowfish and the small fish of the pools
scientificName: Toxotes chatareus; Melanotaenia splendida; Nematalosa erebi; Amniataba percoides

identification.basis: The dictionary names the archerfish in both dialects, a freshwater minnow and two freshwater perches. The Atlas records the seven-spot archerfish, rainbowfish, bony bream, banded grunter and a freshwater sole within 30 km of Karma Waters.

summary: **[mujarrka](word:mujarrka)** in Yalanji and **[dalku](word:dalku)** in Nyungkul is the archerfish, the fish that shoots; **[julba](word:julba)** is the 'fresh water minnow', which on the Mitchell is the rainbowfish and the bony bream, and **[bayil](word:bayil)** and **[dijarr](word:dijarr)** are freshwater perches, the dictionary's words for the small grunters [ref:hershberger1982]. These are the fish that feed the fish: 'small fish (rainbowfish, young grunter, bony bream) feed barramundi, saratoga, mouth almighty and sleepy cod, the darter, the cormorants, the kingfishers, the kites and the crocodiles', as the [waterhole](entry:waterhole) page puts it, and a pool with no small fish in it is a pool with nothing bigger either [ref:ntgov-barra] [ref:wiki-saratoga] [ref:wiki-darter]. The **archerfish** is the one with a trick: the genus was named by Cuvier 'after he noted the "remarkable" ability of these fish to shoot drops of water at insects within reach, making them fall into the water to be eaten'; 'an adult fish almost always hits the target on the first shot' [ref:angfa-archer] [ref:wiki-archerfish-family]. The **rainbowfish** school in the shallows by day, the **bony bream** shoal near the bottom and are 'often the first species to succumb when ephemeral habitats begin to dry up', and the **banded grunter**, 'usually under 10 cm, with a yellowish body crossed by four or five vertical black bands', will eat 'anything resembling food' [ref:wiki-rainbowfish] [ref:wiki-bony-bream] [ref:angfa-banded]. Two snakes live on them: the **Arafura file snake**, a loose-skinned water snake that grows to 2.5 m and preys 'on large fish, such as eel-tailed catfish', and the harmless **keelback**, 'one of the few Australian snakes that can eat cane toads' [ref:wiki-file-snake] [ref:wiki-keelback].

infobox.label: Rainbowfish
infobox.value: Large schools in small streams and the pool shallows; insects and algae

infobox.label: Bony bream
infobox.value: Deep silver body, a long trailing dorsal filament; shoals near the bottom; first to die as a pool dries

infobox.label: Role
infobox.value: The forage base of the pool: food for barramundi, saratoga, sleepy cod, mouth almighty, birds, snakes and crocodiles

sections.heading: Names
sections.body: **[mujarrka](word:mujarrka)** 'archer fish (Yalanji) (Nyungkul - *dalku*)', also glossed 'spotted jewfish, fresh and saltwater, in King's Plains rivers'; **[dalku](word:dalku)** 'archer fish (Nyungkul dialect)'. **[julba](word:julba)** 'fresh water minnow'. **[bayil](word:bayil)** 'fresh water perch'; **[dijarr](word:dijarr)** 'species of fresh water perch'. **[kurrubal](word:kurrubal)** 'fresh water cod' [ref:hershberger1982]. The dictionary's coastal small fish are **[jilngu](word:jilngu)** 'boney salmon, ox eye herring', **[bunjulu](word:bunjulu)** 'giant herring', **[kalngkan](word:kalngkan)** 'small mullet', **[ngalkun](word:ngalkun)** 'mullet' and **[milkaji](word:milkaji)** 'blue tailed mullet', which do not come this far up the Mitchell [ref:hershberger1982].

sections.heading: The small fish of the upper Mitchell
sections.body:
**Seven-spot archerfish** (*Toxotes chatareus*, *mujarrka*, *dalku*), seven records within 60 km. 'They are usually no larger than 20 centimetres but may grow up to 40 centimetres. Unlike most archerfish, *T. chatareus* are sooty rather than silvery in colour. They are omnivorous, feeding on insects, fish, and vegetative matter at the surface of the water. Breeding occurs in the wet season, and 20,000 to 150,000 eggs may be laid at one time'; 'they may live in brackish or fresh water, inhabiting mangrove swamps and estuaries as well as further upstream in slow-moving rivers'; 'white and usually has six or seven dark blotches, alternating long and short, along the dorsal side ... The colour of these blotches may become darker or lighter due to time of day, environment, and stress'; 'weigh up to 700 grams'; 'a lifespan of three to five years' [ref:wiki-archerfish]. It 'is commonly found in brackish estuaries but also ranges well into freshwater, sometimes several hundred kilometres upstream of tidal influence'; 'an intact riparian zone is critical for *Toxotes chatareus*, since it supplies much of its food; inland, it favours deep waterholes fringed with overhanging vegetation, especially *Pandanus*'; 'small juveniles are most often seen around dense macrophyte beds, while adults, being predominantly surface feeders, are usually observed near the surface' [ref:angfa-archer]. The shooting: 'archerfish are remarkably accurate in their shooting; an adult fish almost always hits the target on the first shot'; 'young archerfish start shooting when they are about 2.5 cm long but are inaccurate at first and must learn from experience', hunting 'in small schools' and learning by watching each other [ref:wiki-archerfish-family].

**Rainbowfish** (*Melanotaenia splendida*, *julba*), twenty-one records within 60 km. The *splendida* rainbowfish 'is usually found in large schools inhabiting small freshwater streams, but is also found in lakes and reservoirs'; the Mitchell's form is the Gulf-draining one, the eastern form being 'found in river systems east of the Great Dividing Range' [ref:wiki-rainbowfish]. A finger-long fish with a rainbow sheen down the flank, the male brighter, in the warm shallows over sand and weed.

**Bony bream** (*Nematalosa erebi*), five records. 'A deep bodied, laterally compressed fish with a blunt snout. Spineless dorsal fin with the posterior ray developed into a long filament. Usually silver overall, sometimes grey to greenish dorsally'; 'tends to forms large shoals near the bottom'; found 'mostly in shallow areas of slow flowing or still rivers and streams, especially in turbid conditions'; 'can tolerate water temperatures between 9° and 38°C ... Despite these wide tolerances, bony bream are susceptible to low oxygen levels and are often the first species to succumb when ephemeral habitats begin to dry up'; in the dams they are 'often referred to as "Barra lollies" because of a tendency for impoundment barramundi to round them up' [ref:wiki-bony-bream].

**Banded grunter** (*Amniataba percoides*, the dictionary's freshwater perch), twenty records within 60 km, one within 30. 'The second most widespread of Australia's freshwater grunters, after the spangled perch, *Amniataba percoides* is also one of the smaller and more attractive members of the family, usually under 10 cm, with a yellowish body crossed by four or five vertical black bands of variable width'; it 'will cruise the tank ... searching for anything resembling food', takes 'shrimp, earthworms and small fish with equal enthusiasm' and is an 'excellent jumper' [ref:angfa-banded]. Its big cousins are the [spangled perch](entry:spangled-perch) and the [sooty grunter](entry:black-bream).

**Freshwater sole** (*Brachirus salinarum*), one record: a flatfish of the sand bottom, the one fish here that lies on its side [ref:ala-karma].

**The two fish-eating snakes.** The **Arafura file snake** (*Acrochordus arafurae*), three records within 60 km: 'an aquatic snake species found in northern Australia and New Guinea'; 'adults grow to 2.5 m in length. They have very loose skin and are known to prey on large fish, such as eel-tailed catfish. Females are usually larger than males and they have been known to give birth to up to 17 young' [ref:wiki-file-snake]. The **keelback** or freshwater snake (*Tropidonophis mairii*), one record: 'preys mainly on frogs, but also eats small fishes, lizards, and mammals. It is one of the few Australian snakes that can eat cane toads, up to a certain size, without being harmed' [ref:wiki-keelback].

sections.heading: Telling them
sections.body:
- **Archerfish**: deep-bodied, pointed head, big eyes, dark blotches on a pale side, hanging just under the surface by the overhanging branches [ref:wiki-archerfish].
- **Rainbowfish**: small, slim, iridescent, in a school in the sunlit shallows [ref:wiki-rainbowfish].
- **Bony bream**: silver, deep, a trailing thread off the back of the dorsal fin, in a shoal low down in muddy water [ref:wiki-bony-bream].
- **Banded grunter**: yellowish with four or five black bars, under 10 cm; a young [spangled perch](entry:spangled-perch) is spotted, not barred [ref:angfa-banded].
- **Young sooty grunter, sleepy cod and mouth almighty** are the other small fish; see their pages.
- **File snake**: wrinkled loose skin, a flat head, never on land; the **keelback** is a small brown snake of the water's edge with keeled scales, harmless, and easily mistaken for a [brown snake](entry:snakes), so treat every snake as venomous until it is in the water and swimming [ref:wiki-file-snake] [ref:wiki-keelback] [ref:healthdirect-snakebite].

sections.heading: Signs
sections.body:
- **Rises in the evening** under the branches: saratoga, archerfish and rainbowfish on the insects [ref:angfa-archer] [ref:wiki-saratoga].
- **A spurt of water at a leaf** and an insect falling: the archerfish [ref:wiki-archerfish-family].
- **Schools flickering in the shallows** at midday: rainbowfish, and the [azure kingfisher](entry:kookaburras-and-kingfishers) on the branch above them [ref:wiki-azure-kingfisher].
- **Silver fish dead on the surface** of a shrinking pool: bony bream, the first to go, and the pool's warning [ref:wiki-bony-bream].
- **A big boil near a snag at dusk**: a barramundi into the bony bream [ref:ntgov-barra].

sections.heading: Where they are
sections.body: The archerfish in the deep pools under overhanging pandanus and paperbark; the rainbowfish in the small streams and the sunlit shallows; the bony bream in the slow turbid water low down; the grunters everywhere; the file snake in the deep still water and the keelback at the edge [ref:angfa-archer] [ref:wiki-rainbowfish] [ref:wiki-bony-bream] [ref:wiki-file-snake] [ref:wiki-keelback]. See the [waterhole](entry:waterhole) page for the parts of a pool.

sections.heading: The forage base, by the hour
sections.body: The [waterhole](entry:waterhole) page gives the whole food web; the small fish are its middle. **Day**: the rainbowfish and young grunters graze insects and algae in the warm shallows, the bony bream work the biofilm on the bottom, and the [kingfishers](entry:kookaburras-and-kingfishers), the darter and the cormorants take them from above [ref:jardine2013] [ref:wiki-darter] [ref:wiki-azure-kingfisher]. **Evening**: the insects come down to the water, and the archerfish, rainbowfish and [saratoga](entry:saratoga) rise to them, the archerfish shooting the ones still on the leaves [ref:angfa-archer] [ref:wiki-saratoga]. **Night**: the [mouth almighty](entry:mouth-almighty) and [sleepy cod](entry:sleepy-cod) hunt the small fish by ambush in the dark, the [barramundi](entry:barramundi) rounds up the bony bream, and the file snake and the [crocodile](entry:freshwater-crocodile) hunt in the deep water [ref:ntgov-barra] [ref:wiki-bony-bream] [ref:wiki-file-snake] [ref:webb1982]. **The dry**: as the pool shrinks the bony bream die first, feeding the kites and the crocodile, and the archerfish and grunters hold on in the deepest hole until the first flood, when the archerfish spawns its tens of thousands of eggs [ref:wiki-bony-bream] [ref:wiki-archerfish]. The keelback is the one snake here that profits from the cane toad, eating the small ones unharmed [ref:wiki-keelback] [ref:wiki-cane-toads].

sections.heading: Seasons
sections.body: The archerfish breeds in the wet; the small fish fill the shallows through the early dry; the bony bream die-off is the late-dry sign that a pool is failing [ref:wiki-archerfish] [ref:wiki-bony-bream]. See [the year on country](entry:seasons).

sections.heading: Uses
sections.body:
- **Bait**: the small fish are what the [hooks and lines](entry:hooks-and-lines) for barramundi, sleepy cod and saratoga are baited with [ref:ntgov-barra].
- **Food**: the archerfish is 'occasionally caught and eaten', and a pan of grunters and bony bream is a meal, bony as the name says [ref:wiki-archerfish] [ref:wiki-bony-bream].
- **A net fishery**: the dictionary's **[warrur](word:warrur)** is 'tree bark which can be used as vine. It was used to make fishnets, which were dragged through the water in the dry season when the water goes down', which is small-fish fishing; see [nets](entry:nets) [ref:hershberger1982].
- **Reading the pool**: the small fish are the measure of what the pool holds [ref:wiki-bony-bream].

sections.heading: Netting small fish and reading the archerfish
sections.body:
1. **Watch the shallows at midday** for the rainbowfish schools and the sand bottom for the grunters; that is where to set a small-mesh drag.
2. **The drag net**, as the dictionary's *warrur* describes it: a bark-fibre net 'dragged through the water in the dry season when the water goes down', two people walking it through a shallow bay to the bank; see [nets](entry:nets) and [string and twine](entry:string-and-twine) [ref:hershberger1982].
3. **A scoop or a dilly bag** under the weed edge takes bait fish in a minute; see [dilly bags](entry:dilly-bags).
4. **Keep bait fish alive** in a bucket in the shade; a dead rainbowfish is still bait for a [sleepy cod](entry:sleepy-cod).
5. **For the archerfish**, sit still above a pandanus-fringed pool at evening and watch the leaves; the spurt and the splash are the fish, and a small insect-baited hook dropped where it rose will take it [ref:angfa-archer] [ref:wiki-archerfish-family].
6. **Queensland's rules** on bait nets and sizes are in the [fishing law](entry:hooks-and-lines) page; check them before dragging a net.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body:
- A snake in the water is a snake; the keelback is harmless and the brown snake swims too, so leave both [ref:wiki-keelback] [ref:healthdirect-snakebite].
- The dragging shallows are the crocodile's shallows; see [Crocwise](entry:freshwater-crocodile) [ref:crocwise].
- Queensland's fishing rules apply to nets and bait as to everything else, with native title rights alongside them [ref:alrc] [ref:wyac2020].
- A pool with dead bony bream on it is low in oxygen and going bad; do not drink from it [ref:wiki-bony-bream].

sections.heading: On Country today
sections.body: Every Karma Waters pool has its rainbowfish and its grunters, and the deep ones under the pandanus have the archerfish shooting at evening [ref:ala-karma-60] [ref:angfa-archer]. Which small fish is *julba* and which perch is *bayil* and *dijarr* here is for the contribution box below [ref:hershberger1982].
